item.title: FG Commissions Three CNG Facilities In Kano
item.description: The Federal Government has commissioned three Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) infrastructure facilities in Kano State, as part of efforts to expand access to cleaner and cheaper energy and reduce transportation costs. The facilities, developed by Rolling Energy Limited with support from the Midstream and Downstream Gas Infrastructure Fund (MDGIF), comprise a 300,000-standard cubic metres per day Liquefied Compressed Natural Gas (LCNG) distribution hub and a retail station at Tamburawa, Dawakin Kudu Local Government Area, as well as a 21,000-standard cubic metres per day LCNG daughter and retail station at Hotoro, Tarauni LGA. Speaking at the commissioning ceremony, the Minister of State for Petroleum Resources (Gas), Ekperikpe Ekpo, said the projects represented the Federal Government’s commitment to translating Nigeria’s abundant gas resources into tangible economic benefits for citizens. Ekpo, who was represented by a senior government official, said the facilities would strengthen gas distribution, deepen penetration in Kano and neighbouring communities, support businesses and transportation, and create new economic opportunities. He said the Tamburawa hub would provide integrated LNG storage, regasification and CNG distribution services, including the capacity to supply daughter stations, while the retail outlets would ensure that the product reached consumers directly. “Together, these three facilities demonstrate the complete philosophy of our domestic gas agenda: building the infrastructure to receive and distribute gas, while simultaneously creating the last-mile outlets that make the product accessible to Nigerians,” he said. Ekpo during the opening of two CNG daughter stations capable of dispensing CNG to more than 2,500 vehicles and 50 trucks daily in Kano, on Tuesday, November 10, 2026. The minister said the projects aligned with President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda, which, according to him, seeks to move the country from policy formulation to the delivery of critical infrastructure. “His charge to us is clear: we must move from policies to projects, from plans to infrastructure, and from gas reserves beneath our soil to affordable energy that actually reaches our homes, businesses, industries and transportation systems,” he said. Ekpo added that government was determined to mobilise private sector investment to accelerate the development of the country’s gas infrastructure. He commended Rolling Energy, MDGIF, regulators, investors and other technical partners for their contributions to the projects. Also speaking, the Executive Chairman of the Presidential Initiative on Compressed Natural Gas and Electric Vehicles, Barr. Ismaeel Ahmed, said the expansion of CNG infrastructure across the country showed that investments in the sector were yielding results. item.title: Iran lists Argentina navy, air force as terrorist organisations
item.description: Iran’s foreign ministry on Wednesday designated Argentina’s navy and air force as terrorist organisations, following a similar move by Buenos Aires months earlier. In late March, Argentina designated Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, the ideological arm of the military, as a terror organisation, citing the IRGC’s support for Lebanese militant group Hezbollah. Buenos Aires says the group was involved in a 1994 attack on the AMIA Jewish community centre in Buenos Aires that killed 85 people and injured hundreds more. In 2019, Iran passed a law that could see the country retaliate against any state that designates its military forces as terrorist organisations. Tehran “deems the Argentine Navy and the Argentine Air Force subject to the aforementioned law and its provisions, and designates them as terrorist organisations,” the ministry said in a statement. It was not immediately clear what practical effect the designation would have. Earlier this month, Iran made a similar move designating UK’s MI6 as a hostile group and the country’s Royal Navy and Royal Air Force as terrorist organisations. It came after the UK designated the IRGC as a terror organisation in July. The post Iran lists Argentina navy, air force as terrorist organisations appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: Peace Accord under threat as 26 states, FCT record 109 violations – NPC
item.description: …political violence, fake news dominate breaches as Kaduna, Edo, Enugu emerge flashpoints …gunmen disrupt opposition gatherings, threats of AK-47 attacks, religious intolerance raise fears By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The National Peace Accord signed by political parties ahead of the 2027 general elections is facing an early test, with 26 states and the Federal Capital Territory recording 109 violations in just 10 weeks, raising fears of escalating political violence, intimidation and misinformation as campaigns gather momentum. The National Peace Committee (NPC), in its latest monitoring report covering August 19 to October 27, warned that recurring armed disruptions of political activities, threats by political officeholders and the growing spread of fake political information could undermine peaceful campaigns and threaten the credibility of the 2027 elections. The report identified political violence and thuggery as the leading violations, accounting for 33 incidents, while misinformation and disinformation followed closely with 29 cases. Attacks on political activities and campaign materials accounted for another 19 incidents, while intimidation and threats recorded 15 cases. Kaduna emerged as the state with the highest number of reported violations, recording nine incidents, while Edo, Enugu and the FCT recorded seven each. The committee specifically identified Enugu, Oyo, Edo and Cross River as areas requiring urgent attention over recurring armed disruptions, while Benue and Kogi were flagged over security risks surrounding political convoys and movements. The development comes barely three months after 19 political parties signed the National Peace Accord in Abuja on August 18, committing themselves to peaceful, issue-based campaigns and rejecting violence, threats and intimidation ahead of the elections. Under the electoral timetable released by the Independent National Electoral Commission, presidential and National Assembly elections are scheduled for January 16, 2027, while governorship and state House of Assembly elections will be held on February 6, 2027. Campaigns for the presidential and National Assembly elections commenced on August 19, while those for governorship and State Assembly polls began on September 9. According to the NPC report, the 109 violations recorded within the monitoring period translated to an average of about 11 incidents weekly, with the four leading categories accounting for 96 cases, representing 88 per cent of the total. item.title: Meghan Keeps Low Profile On First Trip After Father’s Arrest
item.description: Meghan Markle appeared in public for the first time Tuesday since her estranged father was charged for alleged possession of child sexual abuse images — keeping a low profile as she visited Brussels with her husband Prince Harry. The Duke and Duchess of Sussex were greeted by a cluster of photographers on arrival at the EU parliament for an event about the dangers children face online. Meghan’s father Thomas Markle was arrested in Florida on Friday and charged with one count of possession of child sexual abuse material — and she did not reply to a shouted question seeking a comment. The couple had been due to give a joint speech, but only Harry spoke at the opening of an installation honouring 50 children who died because of online abuse and exploitation, dubbed the “Lost Screen Memorial”. Britain’s Prince Harry (L), Duke of Sussex and his wife Meghan (R), Duchess of Sussex, arrive at the European Parliament in Brussels on November 10, 2026, to attend the opening of “Lost Screen Memorial”. Photo by JOHN THYS / AFP An unnamed source told the UK’s Daily Telegraph newspaper that Meghan is “just not strong enough emotionally to be doing any public speaking” following her father’s arrest. The couple projected calm when they arrived on Tuesday morning. Dressed in all black with a small poppy pin — the symbol of remembrance for soldiers who died in battle — Meghan held tightly on to Harry’s hand. The duke was dressed in a sombre dark blue suit, also with a poppy and dark-coloured tie. Meghan appeared smiling next to Harry as she met European Parliament President Roberta Metsola and Spanish EU lawmaker Antonio Lopez-Isturiz. The visit also marked the couple’s first appearance together at a public event abroad, since returning to live in Britain following six years in the United States. ‘Disturbing’ allegations Meghan’s 82-year-old father was taken into custody by FBI agents Friday at the retirement home where he lives in Lakeland, Florida and has been ordered to undergo a psychiatric examination. On Tuesday, US Attorney Bill Essayli posted to X that he had requested Thomas Markle be detained because the court ordered him to wear a monitoring device but “he allegedly cut the bracelet off”. US Magistrate Judge Lindsay Griffin ordered Thomas Markle “detained pending the resolution of this case” on Tuesday, writing “the defendant violated the conditions of his pretrial release”. The US Justice Department said Markle allegedly “kept child sexual abuse material (CSAM), including sexually explicit photographs of himself with prepubescent girls, in two Los Angeles-area storage units he rented for nearly two decades”. Markle could face up to 20 years in prison if convicted. British tabloids reported last month that pictures of child sex abuse had been found at Thomas Markle’s former home in the Philippines, allegations later confirmed by police but denied by the duchess’s father. item.title: The Promise And The Proof
item.description: Tinubu is asking for time to complete his reforms. His challengers must explain how they would deliver better results. The most consequential promise from today’s campaign platform concerns something Nigerians can judge without a political analyst: whether the lights stay on. Speaking at the APC rally in Dutse, President Bola Tinubu promised reliable electricity, lower living costs, support for smaller businesses and more jobs if re-elected. These commitments reach directly into the daily calculations of households and enterprises. For the tailor buying fuel, the graduate searching for work and the family stretching its food budget, the question is immediate: how soon will improvement arrive? That question now sits at the centre of Tinubu’s re-election argument. The APC unveiled its second-term manifesto today, defending the administration’s reforms while promising improvements in security, living standards, infrastructure and governance. The campaign is asking Nigerians to connect the disruption of the present with the prospect of a more prosperous future. It is a politically demanding request. Voters must decide whether the government has established a credible foundation for improvement and whether their experience gives them sufficient reason to renew its mandate. A New Manifesto Meets An Existing Record An incumbent’s manifesto arrives with a companion document: the record of the government seeking another term. The APC’s new commitments include additional electricity meters, wider health insurance coverage and a reduction in the number of out-of-school children. Its presentation also promised identifiable delivery responsibilities and public reporting of progress. These are campaign commitments, whose implementation remains to be demonstrated. That creates an opportunity for a more useful election debate. On electricity, candidates should explain how proposed investments would improve supply to homes and businesses. On employment, they should distinguish training places, temporary opportunities and sustained paid work. On education, they should explain how children will enter school, remain there and learn. The opposition has a responsibility here too. Criticism of government performance becomes more persuasive when accompanied by a workable alternative. A promise to make life affordable needs an explanation of costs, funding and consequences. A promise to improve security needs an account of personnel, intelligence, accountability and protection for affected communities. The campaign can now be judged against specific proposals. Nigerians should expect the candidates to defend them. item.title: 2027: Atiku’s Supporters Protest In Abuja Over Court Judgment Voiding Candidacy
item.description: Supporters of the presidential candidate of the African democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, are protesting at the Federal High Court in Abuja, demanding the release of the certified true copy of the judgment by Justice Peter Lifu that nullified his candidacy in the upcoming 2027 general election. Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court in Abuja has sacked the Senator David Mark-led executives of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and invalidated all actions they took on behalf of the party. The actions included the nomination of a former Vice President, Alhaji Atiku Abubakar, as the party’s presidential candidate for the 2027 general elections. Atiku’s supporters protesting in Abuja on Wednesday, November 11, 2026 Atiku, whose name was earlier published by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) as a candidate for the presidential poll, has since chosen a former Governor of Rivers State, Rotimi Amaechi, as his running mate. However, in a judgment delivered on Thursday by Justice Peter Lifu, the court declared illegal the Senator Mark-led Caretaker Committee of the ADC, which organised the primary election that produced Atiku as the party’s presidential flag bearer. The court found merit in a suit brought before it by the aggrieved former National Deputy Chairman (North-East) of the party, Nafiu Bala Gombe. Gombe had approached the court to query the process through which the Senator Mark-led Committee took over the reins of leadership of the party. He maintained that, with the resignation of the former National Chairman, Chief Ralph Nwosu, he (Gombe) was qualified to assume the party’s leadership. Consequently, he, among other things, prayed the court to nullify all actions taken on behalf of the party by the Senator Mark-led leadership. Listed as defendants in the suit, marked FHC/ABJ/CS/1819/2025, were the ADC, INEC, Senator Mark, Ogbeni Rauf Aregbesola and Chief Ralph Nwosu. The plaintiff further urged the court to restrain Senator Mark and Aregbesola from parading themselves as National Chairman and Secretary, respectively, of the ADC, insisting that their emergence violated the party’s constitution and the provisions of the Electoral Act. The court upheld the plaintiff’s claim and granted his reliefs, a verdict that could spark a chain of reactions in the polity, with the presidential election scheduled for January 16, 2027. The ADC has already vowed to appeal the judgment. Reacting to the outcome of the case, the National Welfare Secretary of the ADC, Nkemakolam Ukandu, who was later joined as an interested party in the matter, said the verdict would be challenged at the appellate court. In a development on Wednesday, the aggrieved protesters alleged that the delay in releasing the CTC to Atiku’s counsel is a ploy to deprive him of his rights to appeal the judgment which sacked the former vice president as the presidential candidate of the ADC. item.title: Kudus boost as desperate Ghana seek AFCON redemption
item.description: Troubled Ghana have received a boost with Tottenham Hotspur midfielder Mohammed Kudus available for a must-win Africa Cup of Nations qualifier against Somalia on Thursday. Injuries ruled the 26-year-old out of the 2026 World Cup, and he also missed AFCON losses to the Ivory Coast and the Gambia two months ago. Veteran captain and striker Jordan Ayew, who plays for English second-tier club Sheffield United, is another returnee as Ghana seek redemption after a dismal start in Group C. However, the four-time African champions must do without injured Manchester City winger Antoine Semenyo when they face opponents 130 places lower in the world rankings. The loss to the Ivorians in Abidjan was not unexpected, but the 4-2 defeat at home to the Gambians after building a two-goal lead led to Portuguese coach Carlos Queiroz resigning. Matchdays three and four begin on Thursday and conclude on Tuesday. Countries meet each other at home and away, but Ghana will be at ‘home’ twice due to the security situation in Somalia. Somali preparations at a university stadium in Accra were disrupted when security personnel ordered the squad to move to another location. While Ghana seek six points in Essipong to get back into contention ahead of the final two matchdays next March, co-leaders Ivory Coast and Gambia also meet twice, in Abidjan and Bakau. AFP Sport highlights Ghana, Nigeria, Cape Verde and Tunisia — four teams in trouble after poor starts to qualifying. GHANA Swede Kim Lars Bjorkegren, the coach of the Ghana women’s national team, has been put in temporary charge of the men’s team while the search for a permanent replacement continues. He had mixed results at the recent women’s AFCON in Morocco. They lost to eventual champions Cameroon in the quarter-finals, but are still contenders for the 2027 World Cup in Brazil. After losing narrowly in the Gambia, the Ocean Stars of Somalia held three-time African champions Ivory Coast goalless for 88 minutes before conceding twice. NIGERIA Having struggled to overcome modest Madagascar at home on matchday one in Group L, lacklustre Nigeria crashed to a 3-0 away loss against Guinea-Bissau, a country ranked 124th in the world. On top of failing to qualify for the last two World Cup tournaments, the humiliating AFCON defeat led to an outcry with former star Segun Odegbami lamenting “a dive to new depths”. Nigeria must face Tanzania — auotmatic qualifiers as co-hosts with Kenya and Uganda — without injured star striker Victor Osimhen, the 2023 African Footballer of the Year. CAPE VERDE Football fans at the 2026 World Cup fell in love with the tiny island nation off the west coast of Africa after they held Spain, then took Argentina to extra time in a last-32 tie. But the Blue Sharks could miss a second successive AFCON after losing away to Mali and at home to Rwanda. They now face fellow Group K strugglers Liberia twice. item.title: AFCONQ: Nigeria vs Tanzania – date, time and where to watch
item.description: The Super Eagles of Nigeria will return to action on Friday, November 13, when they host Tanzania in a crucial 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifying encounter. The Group L matchday-three fixture will take place at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, as Nigeria seek to strengthen their chances of qualifying for the continental tournament. The encounter is scheduled to kick off at 5:00 pm Nigerian time (WAT). Nigeria head into the fixture needing a victory after a mixed start to their qualifying campaign, having recorded one win and one defeat in their opening two matches. Where Nigeria stand in Group L The Super Eagles currently occupy second position in Group L with three points from two matches, three points behind leaders Guinea-Bissau, who have won both their opening fixtures. Nigeria opened their campaign with a 2-1 victory over Madagascar in Uyo before suffering a 3-0 defeat to Guinea-Bissau away from home. Tanzania sit third with one point, level with bottom-placed Madagascar, but ahead on goal difference. The stakes are particularly high for Nigeria because Tanzania have already secured automatic qualification for the 2027 tournament as one of the co-hosts alongside Kenya and Uganda. Consequently, Nigeria, Guinea-Bissau and Madagascar are competing for the remaining qualification spot available in the group. A victory over Tanzania would take Nigeria to six points and strengthen their position in the race for qualification. Where to watch Nigeria vs Tanzania Football fans in Nigeria can follow the encounter live on SuperSport. When is the return fixture? Nigeria will travel to Tanzania for the return fixture on Tuesday, November 17, as both countries meet again in quick succession. The two encounters could prove important for Nigeria’s qualification ambitions, with the Super Eagles needing to collect maximum points to avoid falling further behind Guinea-Bissau. The 2027 Africa Cup of Nations will be staged across Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda from June 19 to July 17, 2027. item.title: Fight or flight? Trump mixes signals after midterms
item.description: President Donald Trump’s political mantra is “fight, fight, fight.” But he has given decidedly mixed messages about whether he will do so after Republicans were hammered in the midterms. In the week since becoming a lame duck, Trump named the hardline architect of his migration crackdown as his chief of staff, while admitting his deportation policy was too tough. The 80-year-old raised eyebrows when he publicly asked Ultimate Fighting Championship boss Dana White to be his new press secretary — then claimed he was just joking. He has admitted that the Iran war was largely to blame for the midterms rout. But he has strongly backed Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth’s battle against impeachment. And despite saying on election night that he’d accept the results of the Democratic sweep, he has reverted to type and revived baseless claims of election fraud. “One of the characteristics of Donald Trump is that he changes his mind on a dime,” Democratic Senator Chris Coons told CNN. “He’ll be praising someone on Monday, firing them on Tuesday, and pretending he never knew them on Wednesday. So it’s hard to predict exactly what Donald Trump is going to do.” – ‘Too tough’ – Democrats have promised to rein in Trump and launch a series of investigations into corruption and abuse of power. He could face a third impeachment. But for a president supposedly facing his last stand, he has at times struck a surprisingly conciliatory tone. As results came in, he congratulated Democrats on seizing Congress and said he could work with them. Instead of a press conference the next day, he gave reporters a tour of his new White House ballroom — sparking speculation he might spend the rest of his term on his building projects. But the signs of volatility were still there. In the Oval Office, Trump placed a red baseball cap saying “veto” on his desk. And when Trump announced on Friday that ultraloyalist Stephen Miller would replace Susie Wiles as his chief of staff, it seemed that the gloves were finally off. The brains behind the masked immigration raids that left two Americans dead, Miller has also been instrumental in using executive orders to help Trump bypass Congress. Yet in an interview the same day — though broadcast on Sunday — Trump conceded voters had been turned off by the aggressive deportation push. “I think it was too tough,” Trump told the CBS News “60 Minutes” program. Still, the chances of Trump doing a deal with Democrats — possibly even for an amnesty for undocumented migrants — remain low. “It doesn’t seem likely. Not with this decision to have Stephen Miller running the show,” Sarah Binder, a senior fellow in governance studies at the Brookings Institution, said in a panel discussion this week. – ‘Violent fighter’ – Trump’s astonishing announcement on Saturday that he wanted “violent fighter and warrior” Dana White to be his new spokesman also seemed to signal a war footing. If it seemed too ironic to be true, it was. A day later Trump said he was “kidding.”

item.title: Tinubu’s Economic Reforms Financing New Era Of State Infrastructure, Says Keyamo
item.description: The Aviation Minister, Festus Keyamo, has drawn a direct connection between President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms, improved state revenues and the emergence of major infrastructure projects. Keyamo, who spoke at the groundbreaking of Kogi State’s international cargo airport on Tuesday, said the development represented something larger than the commencement of another airport project. According to him, it was an opportunity to explain how President Tinubu’s economic reforms are reshaping the financial capacity of state governments and creating opportunities for infrastructure development. Speaking at Zariagi in Adavi Local Government Area, where he represented the President at the ceremony, Keyamo attributed the project’s commencement to a combination of federal economic policies and the development priorities of Kogi State Governor Ahmed Usman Ododo. “What is happening here today, what the Governor has done today, will resonate many, many years, centuries after today, 500 years from today. Do you understand the significance of what is happening here today? Let me tell you the significance. Today, as from today, this village called Zariagi will be on the Global Aviation Map,” the Minister declared. According to Keyamo, the combination of national economic reform and purposeful state leadership was central to the airport initiative. Keyamo flags off Kogi Int’l Airport construction. Since assuming office in May 2023, President Tinubu has introduced major economic policy changes, including the removal of petrol subsidy and reforms to Nigeria’s foreign exchange system. The measures have been accompanied by significant economic pressures, particularly higher living costs and exchange-rate volatility. However, the administration has also argued that the reforms are intended to reduce longstanding fiscal distortions, improve government finances and create a more sustainable foundation for investment. Keyamo linked those changes to the growing financial capacity of state governments. He argued that the development requires leadership capable of converting available resources into productive investments. The Kogi airport project is intended to strengthen the state’s position in transportation, logistics, agriculture and commercial development. Speaking at the event, Governor Ododo noted that the infrastructure of the proposed airport was capable of improving access to domestic and international markets while attracting businesses and investors. Describing the airport project as a strategic investment in the economic future of Kogi State, Ododo emphasised its potential to unlock the state’s enormous agricultural and solid mineral resources for local and international markets. item.title: US House blocks impeachment bid against Hegseth over Iran war
item.description: Republicans in the US House of Representatives on Tuesday blocked an effort to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth over the Iran war, handing President Donald Trump a victory days after his party’s crushing midterm election defeat. The House voted 211 to 204 to send the impeachment resolution to the Judiciary Committee, effectively derailing a planned vote Wednesday on whether to bring formal charges against the embattled Pentagon chief. The resolution was introduced by Republican Thomas Massie, a Trump critic who was the only member of his party to oppose the procedural maneuver, according to US media. The impeachment drive had threatened to deepen Trump’s troubles after Democrats swept last week’s midterms, with anger at the sputtering Iran war and soaring fuel prices helping drive voters to a historic rejection of Republicans. Republicans still hold a narrow House majority until January, when Democrats take control of both chambers of Congress. And 11 Democrats missed the vote. Trump hailed the procedural defeat as an “EXONERATION of a Great American Patriot,” in a post on Truth Social, while Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell, in a post on X, called the vote as a “TOTAL VICTORY!” “We look forward to ending this sham impeachment in the committee room, where facts will continue to prevail and this distraction can be put to rest,” Parnell added. Hegseth earlier Tuesday dismissed the impeachment effort as a “farce” and defended his record leading the Iran war and other military operations under Trump. “It’s a farce, and it’s a stunt, and everybody knows it,” he said at a Pentagon press conference, branding the accusations “slander” and “sabotage.” Moments after Hegseth’s televised appearance, Trump signaled his support. “Pete Hegseth gets an ‘A’ PLUS, PLUS, PLUS,” the 80-year-old president wrote on his Truth Social platform. Vice President JD Vance also backed the defense secretary, saying he had “obviously not” committed impeachable offenses. – ‘Would do it again’ – Massie’s eight articles of impeachment accused Hegseth of illegally waging war without congressional authorization and abusing his powers as Pentagon chief. Several related to the eight-month Iran war, accusing him of violating the War Powers Resolution, which places limits on US military interventions without congressional authorization. Other allegations involved the 2025 conflict with Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis and strikes on alleged drug-smuggling boats in the Caribbean and eastern Pacific, which Massie branded “extrajudicial killings.” He also accused Hegseth of suppressing free speech by trying to punish Democratic Senator Mark Kelly over a video urging military and intelligence personnel to refuse illegal orders. item.title: Police arrest Abuja man over alleged rape, cyberbullying of women
item.description: The Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Police Command has arrested a man, identified as Usman Mohammed, over alleged rape, sexual assault, cyberbullying and intimidation of women under the pretext of recovering debts owed to him. The Police Public Relations Officer, SP Josephine Adeh, disclosed this in a statement, saying the suspect allegedly targeted women, including widows and other vulnerable persons, through predatory money-lending practices. Adeh said the suspect was arrested on Friday, November 6, 2026, following a report received at the Lugbe Police Station at about 7:05 p.m., alleging that he had been intimidating, sexually assaulting and physically assaulting several women over debts owed to him. She said operatives from the Lugbe Division, led by the Divisional Police Officer, immediately launched efforts to track down the suspect. According to her, the suspect was traced to the Federal Housing Authority (FHA), Lugbe, where police operatives moved to arrest him. However, he allegedly attempted to escape upon sighting the officers by speeding off in his vehicle. The police said the operatives gave chase and eventually intercepted him before he could gain access to the expressway. Adeh said preliminary investigations identified Mohammed as a resident of FHA Lugbe, who allegedly used debt recovery as a pretext to intimidate and exploit his victims. She alleged that, in his latest incident, the suspect lured a woman into his vehicle and drove her to a secluded location in Lugbe, where he sexually assaulted and raped her. The suspect allegedly forced the victim to strip naked and recorded videos of her private parts, which he subsequently used to threaten to expose her publicly and kill her if she failed to meet his repayment demands. The police spokesperson said Mohammed was currently in custody and undergoing further interrogation. She added that he would be charged to court upon the conclusion of investigations. The Commissioner of Police, FCT Command, CP Ahmed Muhammed Sanusi, condemned all forms of violence, sexual exploitation, intimidation and cyberbullying. He urged residents, particularly vulnerable persons, not to suffer in silence but to report cases of abuse, threats, blackmail and other criminal activities to the nearest police station. The Command also provided emergency contact numbers for members of the public: 08032003913 and 08061581938. item.title: CNG to save Kano tricycle riders ₦8,200 daily — MDGIF
item.description: Commercial tricycle operators in Kano State could save about ₦8,200 daily on fuel costs by switching from petrol to Compressed Natural Gas (CNG), the Executive Director of the Midstream and Downstream Gas Infrastructure Fund (MDGIF), Oluwole Adama, has said. Adama disclosed this on Tuesday during the commissioning of two Liquefied Compressed Natural Gas (LCNG) facilities established by the MDGIF in partnership with Rolling Energy Limited in Kano. He explained that an operator who spends about ₦14,200 daily on 10 litres of petrol would spend approximately ₦6,000 on CNG for the equivalent energy, resulting in a daily saving of ₦8,200. According to him, the savings could amount to nearly ₦250,000 monthly, providing tricycle operators with additional income to meet household expenses, pay their children’s school fees and save towards owning their tricycles. “Here in Kano, a litre of petrol sells for about ₦1,420, while the same amount of energy from CNG costs about ₦600. That is less than half the price,” Adama said. The two facilities commissioned are the LCNG Mother Station at Tamburawa and a Daughter Station at Hotoro Quarters in Tarauni Local Government Area. Adama said the facilities could support the refuelling of up to 2,500 cars and tricycles daily, while also supplying gas to other refuelling stations. He added that they could serve up to 200 trucks daily, helping to reduce transportation costs and ease the movement of goods from Kano to other parts of the country. The MDGIF executive director disclosed that the Tamburawa Mother Station had the capacity to handle 300,000 standard cubic metres of gas daily. He urged fleet owners, transport unions, businesses and investors to take advantage of the facilities, while calling on Rolling Energy to maintain high safety standards and ensure reliable services. Earlier, the Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Rolling Energy Limited, Mubarak Umar Danbatta, said the projects would bring gas supply closer to businesses and investors in Northern Nigeria. He explained that the development would reduce the cost and logistical challenges associated with transporting gas over long distances, making it easier for businesses to establish CNG stations and industries that depend on natural gas. Danbatta said his company previously travelled hundreds of kilometres from Abuja to source CNG from Ajaokuta and Obajana in Kogi State before transporting it to supply its stations. “What Rolling Energy and MDGIF are doing here in Kano is changing that model. We are bringing gas closer to the people,” he said. He disclosed that the Tamburawa facility had a designed gas-handling capacity of five million standard cubic feet daily, with two LNG storage tanks of 55 metric tonnes each, while the Hotoro station had a storage capacity of eight metric tonnes. item.title: Kidnappers: I’ll sign execution warrant even for my father – Okpebholo
item.description: Edo State Governor, Monday Okpebholo, has vowed to sign the death warrants of convicted kidnappers, regardless of their relationship with him, declaring that he would personally supervise their execution. The governor said he would not spare anyone found guilty of kidnapping, even if the convict were his father or a close family member. Okpebholo spoke in a video shared by TheCable on Tuesday, amid efforts by his administration to enforce the state’s law prescribing the death penalty for kidnapping offences resulting in the death of victims. “I pray our brothers are not involved because I will sign it. Even if it is my father, I will sign it. The truth is this: we just have to get some bad elements out of the system for the system to stand. “Because somebody will die. But these people are the ones killing people. How many people have we killed?” he said. The governor defended the proposed executions by highlighting the trauma and physical injuries suffered by victims of kidnapping. He cited an incident involving a woman who was allegedly pushed during an abduction attempt, saying the fear and trauma she experienced could have resulted in her death. He also referred to an attack on the state’s Chief Judge, who he said sustained serious injuries, including the loss of the use of one hand, during an encounter with kidnappers. “Just look at the way they were pushing that woman down there. Supposing she died at that, because of fear, only fear. It’s enough for her to die. People have gone through trauma. “Even our Chief Judge, if you see our Chief Judge, one of his hands was cut off by kidnappers,” he added. Okpebholo said he had contacted the state Attorney-General to ascertain the status of the relevant documents and was awaiting further action. He, however, vowed to pursue the cases through the appeal process, insisting that convicted kidnappers would not be allowed to escape punishment. “But we still follow them up on the appeal. We won’t just let them go like that. So we will get to wherever they stop, we will take them from there. We will not spare anybody. “I stand, if I see this paper today, now, I will sign it and I will even supervise the killing,” he said. The governor’s comments come amid the implementation of the Edo State Kidnapping Prohibition (Amendment) Law, 2025, which introduced the death penalty for kidnapping offences resulting in the death of victims. The Edo State House of Assembly passed the amendment in February 2025, and Okpebholo signed it into law later that month. Under the amended law, kidnapping offences in which victims survive attract life imprisonment, while those directly involved in abductions resulting in the death of victims face capital punishment. The law also prescribes penalties for individuals who aid, abet or provide support for kidnapping activities. item.title: Nearly 64,000 Nigerians flee to Niger over insecurity — UNHCR
item.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo Nearly 64,000 Nigerians have fled their homes and crossed into neighbouring Niger Republic since the beginning of 2026 to escape escalating violence involving Islamist militants and armed criminal gangs, the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) has said. The UN refugee agency, in a briefing issued on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, warned that the influx was worsening an already difficult humanitarian situation in Niger, which hosts more than 500,000 refugees and asylum-seekers. According to the agency, approximately 327,500 Nigerians are already seeking refuge in Niger, while several hundred others have reportedly crossed into neighbouring Benin Republic because of deteriorating security conditions in northern Nigeria. UNHCR’s Director of External Relations, Dominique Hyde, said most of the newly arrived Nigerians had settled in the border regions of Diffa, in southeastern Niger, and Tahoua, in the western part of the country. The agency disclosed that about 1,200 Nigerians crossed into Diffa in October, while another 3,400 arrived in Tahoua during the same period. It added that more than 23,000 people, over two-thirds of them children, had arrived in Diffa since the beginning of the year. UNHCR expressed concern over the harsh living conditions confronting displaced families, many of whom are staying in makeshift shelters without adequate food, clean drinking water, healthcare and other essential services. Some women, it said, were forced to walk several kilometres daily to fetch water for their families, while humanitarian organisations had reported rising cases of malnutrition, respiratory infections and poor sanitation among the new arrivals. The agency also raised concerns over the registration of displaced Nigerians, disclosing that only about five per cent of those who arrived in Niger this year had been formally registered. It warned that the lack of proper documentation was making it difficult for thousands of refugees to access humanitarian assistance and essential public services. The humanitarian crisis, according to UNHCR, is further compounded by insecurity and climate-related challenges in Niger, particularly in Diffa, where more than 70 per cent of the country’s reported security incidents this year have occurred. Despite the growing pressure, the agency acknowledged the support of Niger’s authorities and host communities, including the provision of land for temporary shelters. However, it appealed for increased international assistance, seeking $11.4 million to expand its humanitarian response in Niger, Nigeria and Benin. The appeal includes $2 million for urgent interventions covering food, water, shelter, healthcare, refugee registration and protection. UNHCR warned that without additional funding, thousands of vulnerable families fleeing violence could be left without access to essential humanitarian assistance. item.title: NERC approves N30bn for free meters, targets May 2027
item.description: The Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC) has approved N30 billion for the third tranche of the Meter Acquisition Fund (MAF), targeting the provision of free electricity meters to all remaining unmetered Band A customers and accelerated metering of Band B customers. The Commission announced the approval in Order No. NERC/2026/121 on the operationalisation of Tranche C of the MAF, which took effect on November 2, 2026. Under the arrangement, the N30 billion will be allocated among the 11 electricity Distribution Companies (DisCos) in proportion to their respective contributions to the fund. NERC said the third tranche was designed to accelerate efforts to close Nigeria’s metering gap, with equitable distribution of meters across states within the respective DisCo franchise areas. The Commission directed the DisCos to conduct transparent procurement processes involving eligible Local Meter Manufacturers and Assemblers (LMMAs) and Meter Asset Providers (MAPs) with verified meter stocks. It said maximum procurement prices had been set based on the median national MAP online bid prices recorded during the September 2026 bid cycle. The order provides for payment to selected meter providers in two stages: 70 per cent upon verification of meter stock delivery and the remaining 30 per cent after confirmation of complete installation. NERC emphasised that all meters supplied and installed under the MAF programme must be provided to customers free of charge. It also directed that each meter must prominently display the name of the relevant DisCo, the applicable MAF tranche and the inscription, “NOT FOR SALE”. The Commission further stipulated that where a DisCo initiates the relocation of an existing customer’s connection point for revenue protection purposes, the cost must be borne by the distribution company. It warned that sanctions would apply where defaults by DisCos impede or delay meter installation. To ensure transparency and accountability, the order also establishes monitoring, reporting and evaluation requirements for the Fund Manager, DisCos and participating meter providers. All supply and installation contracts under Tranche C are required to be filed with the Commission, while the installation of all meters under the tranche must be completed on or before May 31, 2027. NERC urged electricity distribution companies and other stakeholders to comply strictly with the order, describing the initiative as part of efforts to close the national metering gap, strengthen revenue assurance, improve service delivery and protect electricity consumers. item.title: Anambra to prioritise erosion control in environmentally responsible communities
item.description: By Vincent Ujumadu The Anambra State Government has resolved to prioritise communities that demonstrate environmental responsibility in its interventions to control erosion across the state. The decision was taken at the weekly State Executive Council (EXCO) meeting in Awka, where the government said communities engaging in practices that worsen erosion would no longer receive priority attention. The prohibited practices include sand excavation, indiscriminate felling of trees, deforestation, dumping of refuse in drainage channels and directing stormwater onto roads. The State Commissioner for Information and Value Reformation, Dr Law Mefor, who disclosed this after the meeting, said perpetrators of such practices would also be prosecuted to serve as a deterrent to others. Anambra has more than 1,000 active erosion sites affecting communities across the state, with experts arguing that addressing the scale of the problem would require federal and international intervention. Also at the meeting, the EXCO directed that Ogbodi in Amichi community, Nnewi South Local Government Area, which was recently cut off by gully erosion, should be reconnected within two weeks through palliative measures. Mefor said the process of identifying a permanent solution to the erosion problem would commence immediately. The erosion had cut off Ogbodi residents from other parts of Amichi, disrupting access and movement within the community. Meanwhile, the State EXCO approved what it described as the “Soludozie Anambra Framework”, an organised and inclusive platform designed to promote development through the Public-Private-Community Partnership (PPCP) model. According to Mefor, the initiative is intended to provide a structured channel through which Anambra indigenes at home and in the diaspora, as well as other well-meaning individuals, can partner with the state government to drive development. He explained that under the framework, the government’s role would generally be limited to documentation, recognition and support where requested, while donors and partners would directly manage their funds and projects. Mefor said the initiative was aimed at positioning Anambra as a model of collective governance and inclusive development, while accelerating the state’s development.
